verdictReason: Edge not real: official paid listings are not live (free-only beta, selected creators first, no date, fee set per upload and unpublished) and the in-editor store is open to any approved seller, while itch.io and Getly already sell Godot add-ons. Demand is thin: best paid editor tool found has 24 itch ratings since 2023, 86.8% of poll respondents are hobbyists, mainstream add-ons are free MIT. Year 1 bottom-up: ~$1.4k gross, ~+$150 profit for ~1,300 h; pessimistic -$1.1k.

answers.question: When, and on what eligibility and fee terms, will the official Godot Asset Store open paid listings beyond a select group?
answers.answer: No date is published. The roadmap page read on 2026-10-10 still says the beta allows only free assets, that paid assets start with a certain group of creators, and that charging will later open to everyone. Godot 4.7 shipped the store on 2026-06-19 and about 3.7 months later paid listings were still not described as open. The store's Terms of Service already contemplate selling (Foundation takes a net commission 'specified when uploading the content', sellers use third-party payment providers), but no commission rate or eligibility rule is published; a 5-20% figure is only a community suggestion. Public pages cannot give a date, so an entrant cannot plan revenue from this channel within 365 days.

answers.question: Do Godot developers buy paid add-ons at volume?
answers.answer: No evidence of volume was found, and the little there is points small. The most prominent paid Godot editor tool found on the itch.io top sellers page (AssetPlacer, $26.99, devlogs since Sep 2023) shows 24 total ratings. If 5-20% of buyers rate (assumption, unverified) that is roughly 4-15 sales per month for the flagship. 86.8% of 2025 poll respondents are hobbyists and only 4.7% are studio employees. A developer of a paid Unity tool says he is unsure users will pay for Godot assets, and a $5 Godot AI add-on reported about 200 downloads with a commenter preferring a free open-source rival.

answers.question: Do free or cheap alternatives already cover the wedge (paid editor tools and gameplay systems)?
answers.answer: Largely yes for mainstream categories. The Asset Library lists over 5,000 add-ons; a 2026 roundup of the best Godot plugins lists ten free MIT plugins (LimboAI, Dialogic 2, GUT, Phantom Camera, Terrain3D and others) and one AI product with a free tier. A free MIT 'Godot Asset Placer' duplicates the function of the paid AssetPlacer. A free open-source MCP server competes with a paid one. AI coding assistants ($20/month) make in-house DIY cheaper. Paid add-ons survive only where a buyer values time over price.

answers.question: Is the claimed edge (in-editor discovery plus accumulated ratings) exclusive or compounding for a new entrant?
answers.answer: Not exclusive: every approved seller gets the same in-editor listing, and paid sales already work on itch.io (10% default share) and Getly (80-90% seller share, no approval queue, marketing claim). The compounding part (ratings, update history) favours incumbents with years of ratings (AssetPlacer since 2023), not a 150-day-late entrant. Access for an unknown entrant is unconfirmed because the first paid group is selected. Falsifier: official terms published with open enrolment and a public sales datapoint showing several hundred dollars per month per mid-tier add-on.

answers.question: What do bottom-up first-365-days economics look like for the reference entrant (150 days to first revenue, 25 h/week, $3,000)?
answers.answer: Base: 3 add-ons live from day 150 and 5 from day 250 (about 28.8 add-on-months), 4 sales per add-on-month (low end of the flagship-derived range, so generous to a new unrated seller), $12 realised price, 15.4% fees (itch 10% + 2.9% + $0.30), $1,020 fixed cash costs. Gross $1,381, costs $1,233, profit about +$148 for about 1,300 owner hours. Pessimistic (price x0.8, volume x0.5, costs x1.5): gross $552, costs $1,663, profit about -$1,110. An optimistic sensitivity (10 sales per add-on-month, $15) gives about +$2,650, still low for 1,300 hours.

killReasons.reason: The claimed edge is not available: official paid listings are not live (free-only beta, selected creators first, no date), the commission is set per upload and unpublished, and the same in-editor listing would go to every approved seller, so it is neither exclusive nor confirmed for an unknown entrant within 365 days. Paid sales already work off-store (itch.io, Getly).

Demand and volume are thin: the best paid Godot editor tool found has 24 total ratings since 2023, 86.8% of poll respondents are hobbyists, and a paid-tool developer doubts users will pay for Godot assets.

Free or near-free alternatives cover the mainstream categories: the leading plugins are free MIT, a free MIT clone exists for the paid AssetPlacer, and a free MCP server rivals the paid one; AI assistants cheapen DIY.
Bottom-up economics fail the pessimistic case (about -$1,110) and the base case is about +$148 for roughly 1,300 owner hours, so even the base case is not a viable income.

Pirating or redistributing GDScript add-ons is trivial (source is shipped), and the Foundation's ToS gives it a broad licence over listed content, may remove content at its discretion and is not the seller, leaving payment processing and tax to the provider.

assumptions: assumption: first revenue at day 150, so a 215-day selling window; 3 add-ons live from day 150 and 5 from day 250 (about 150 h each at 25 h/week), giving about 28.8 add-on-months.
assumption: only itch.io (and similar) revenue counts; official-store paid revenue is excluded because no date, fee or eligibility is published.

assumption: 4 sales per add-on-month in the base case. Anchor: the flagship AssetPlacer shows 24 ratings over about 32 months (GAM-3-D13); if 5-20% of buyers rate (assumption, unverified) it sells about 4-15 per month, so 4 is the low end for a flagship and generous for a new unrated seller.
assumption: realised price $12 (observed itch.io list prices about $3-$33, frequent discounts; GAM-3-D11, D12, D16).
sourced: fees 10% itch default (D9) plus 2.9% + $0.30 card processing (D10) = 15.4% at $12; assumption that these stack as modelled.
assumption: fixed cash costs $1,020 = $60/month (AI assistant ~$20 (D21), domain/hosting, tooling) plus $300 one-off bookkeeping/tax setup.
revenue365 is gross sales ($1,381); cost365 includes platform/processor fees ($213) plus fixed costs ($1,020); owner labour of about 1,300 h is unpaid and not costed.
pessimistic: price x0.8 = $9.60, volume x0.5 = 2 per add-on-month, costs x1.5: gross $552, costs $1,663, profit about -$1,110.
sensitivity (not used for verdict): 10 sales per add-on-month at $15 gives gross $4,315 and profit about +$2,650.

legalNotes: Godot Asset Store ToS (GAM-3-D4, D5): Foundation takes a net commission specified at upload (rate unpublished, non-refundable), providers must use third-party payment services (PayPal/Stripe), the Foundation is not the seller, may withhold taxes and may remove content at its sole discretion; providers grant it a broad worldwide sublicensable licence. Paid listing is available only 'if the Foundation offers that option'.

Seller tax and VAT/sales-tax duties for a stranger selling digital goods internationally are not settled on public pages read here; the ToS says VAT is deducted from amounts due to providers. Treat as an unquantified compliance cost.

itch.io: 10% default share (adjustable 0-100%), card fees $0.30 + 2.9%, revenue held 7 days, $5 minimum payout, payout review typically 10-14 days (GAM-3-D9, D10). Getly terms are the company's own marketing claims; its own page warns that marketplaces change terms.

Godot is MIT licensed, so selling add-ons is permitted, but GDScript add-ons ship as readable source and licence enforcement against redistribution is impractical; any reused third-party code must be compatible with commercial resale.
No logins, signups, purchases or contact were made; all findings are from public pages read once each.
unverified: Date, fee and eligibility rules for official paid listings (not published on any page read).
Any real sales or revenue figure for a paid Godot add-on; the 4-15 per month flagship range depends on an unverified 5-20% rating rate.
Whether itch.io ratings are limited to purchasers, and how many ratings a typical sale produces.
Getly's real Godot traffic and sales (only marketing claims read) and how itch.io, Getly and the Godot store handle VAT and sales tax for the seller.
Quotes were taken from page-fetch extractions; the roadmap and ToS pages are undated, so the status 'free-only' is as of the read on 2026-10-10 but not date-stamped by the site.
Whether the new store shows download counts for listings (the one listing read showed none).
nextStep: Do not pursue unless the Godot Foundation publishes open paid-listing enrolment with a fee rate and a public seller-revenue datapoint; re-check store.godotengine.org/roadmap then.
